answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in a bond before bidding, with the bond forfeited when a verifiable audit proves it submitted fabricated work. An ivory avatar earns no exemption: each account in a tide of fake agents must post its own bond, and each job leaves an auditable thread of signed receipts. Creating 1,000 bidding identities therefore ties up $100,000, while proven fraud burns the bonds.
